1.
No one appeared for the petitioners in any of the writ petitions.
2. Sri Ramendra Pratap Singh, learned counsel is present for the Greater NOIDA.
3. As the similar issue is involved in all the writ petitions, they are being decided together by a common order.

4. The relevant prayers in Writ-C No.16574 of 2017 read as under:
"I. a writ, order or direction in the nature of certiorari quashing the award dated 4.8.2011 passed by the respondent no.3 under Section 11(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 in Case No.95 of 2007 in respect of notifications issued under Section 4(1)
read wit6h Section 17(4) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 dated 12.3.2008 and under Section 6 read with Section 17(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 dated 11.7.2008 (Annexure No.3 to this writ petition).
II. a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus commanding the respondent no.3 to pass an appropriate order on the representation of petitioner dated 28.7.2016 and may provide the compensation of the land of Khata No.305, Khasra No.222 area 0.7863 hectare and Khata No.306, Khasra No.167 area 1.9890 hectare situated in Prakash vs State Of U.P. And 3 Othrs. on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92774720/
3 Village Sirsa, Tehsil Sadar, District Gautam Budh Nagar to the petitioner at the rate of compensation determine by the respondent no.2 in Arbitration Award dated 16.5.2016 in respect of the land of petitioner's village acquired for the National Highway Authority of India by issuing notifications dated 14.8.2006, 14.82007 and 28.12.2011, within time bound period which may be fixed by this Hon'ble Court."
5.
Similar prayers have been made in all the connected writ petitions.

6. Learned counsel appearing for the Greater NOIDA submitted that the petitioners in this bunch had received compensation under the Uttar Pradesh Land Acquisition Karar Niyamawali, 1997 (hereinafter referred to as "Karar Niyamawali") and, as such, they cannot dispute the determination made under the award dated 4.8.2011.

entities.text: Uttar Pradesh Land Acquisition Karar Niyamawali, 1997
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 7. From the averments made in the writ petitions, it transpired that the petitioners herein claim that they being innocent farmers had been coerced/misrepresented/duped to sign the documents in the prescribed form of Karar Niyamawali to receive compensation.
The contention, thus, is that the award dated 4.8.2011 is a result of fraud committed by the competent authority.
8. The question of fraud cannot be examined by this Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India as it would require factual enquiry.
In case of any such grievance, the remedy before the petitioners was to file civil suit.
In any case, the validity of the award dated 4.8.2011 prepared under Karar Niyamawali cannot be looked into by this Court.
9. No relief, as such, can be granted.
All the writ petitions in this bunch, are, accordingly, dismissed.
